newquay-fistral.airport: NQY — Newquay (Cornwall), ~15 min; from London ~5 h by train

busua-ghana.description: A quiet fishing village with a long sandy beach and Ghana's top surf spot. South Atlantic swells arrive almost year-round, best and biggest from May to September; in the dry season the waves are smaller and softer. The water is 23–28 °C, so you can surf without a wetsuit, and there are reefs nearby for more experienced surfers.
busua-ghana.rating_basis: Ghana's main surf hub: a gentle wave for learning, warm water and plenty of camps (Surf Atlas, momondo, Culture Trip); Surf-forecast rates the break itself modestly (3/10, “fairly consistent”), with the quality waves on the neighbouring reefs of Dixcove and Butre
busua-ghana.hazards: Rocks at the edges of the bay and reefs at neighbouring spots, rip currents (especially at Butre), malaria — prophylaxis needed
busua-ghana.crowd_note: Lots of students from local schools and camps at the beach, but the line-up is hardly ever crowded; the neighbouring reefs are often empty
busua-ghana.region: Western Region, Gulf of Guinea (Gold Coast)
busua-ghana.area_breaks: Reef and point breaks at the edges of Busua bay (experienced surfers), Butre (further east, bigger, but closes out and has currents), Dixcove / Fort Metal Cross (powerful right over reef, not for beginners), Cape Three Points (soft, slow wave, ~25 km)
busua-ghana.beginner_months: Year-round on Busua's sandy beach (sheltered by rocks to the west, waves often chest-high and soft); in the dry season (November–March) the waves are smaller — ideal for first lessons
pros: Warm water year-round
Gentle waves for learning, inexpensive schools and camps
Hardly any crowds
Vibrant West African culture
cons: The beach itself has a wave of modest quality
Long trip from Accra (4–5 h)
Malaria zone, rainy season in May–June
Little good board rental outside Busua
busua-ghana.airport: ACC — Accra, ~4–5 h by car; TKD — Takoradi (domestic flights), ~40 min

bali-canggu-batu-bolong.description: Canggu is Bali's main surf-tourism hub for beginners and intermediates. At Batu Bolong a gently sloping sand-and-rock bottom produces long, soft peaks breaking left and right, especially on mid and high tide; nearby are Old Man's and the more powerful Berawa and Echo Beach. All around there are dozens of schools, including Russian-speaking ones, board rental on the beach, cafés and co-working spaces.
bali-canggu-batu-bolong.rating_basis: Bali's main “school” and longboard zone: guides (Bali Surfing Camp, Rapture, bali.com) call it the best start for beginners and intermediates, with long, soft waves on the tide. Downsides in reviews: very crowded, lots of beginners and loose boards
bali-canggu-batu-bolong.hazards: Crowds of beginners and loose longboards, rocks and reef in places on the bottom, shorebreak at the north end of the beach, polluted water after heavy rain (run-off), currents when the waves are big
bali-canggu-batu-bolong.crowd_note: Batu Bolong and Old Man's are packed with schools and longboarders all day; Berawa, Echo Beach and Pererenan are quieter, but the waves there are punchier
bali-canggu-batu-bolong.region: Southwest coast of Bali (Canggu), Indian Ocean
bali-canggu-batu-bolong.area_breaks: Nearby: Old Man's (soft reef, longboarding), Berawa (beach break, shortboards), Echo Beach (reef, left/right, intermediate+), Pererenan (reef and beach), Seseh / Canggu Rights; 20–30 min away — Kuta and Legian beaches for first lessons
bali-canggu-batu-bolong.beginner_months: Year-round: schools teach on the soft peaks of Batu Bolong and Berawa, and on the sandy beach at Kuta. Best in April–October (morning offshore); in January–February it's often onshore and the water turns murky after downpours
pros: Soft waves for learning and longboarding
A huge choice of schools, including Russian-speaking ones
Board rental right on the beach
Waves almost every day
cons: Very crowded in the water and on the roads
Closes out at low tide
Onshore in the rainy season and murky water after downpours
Shorebreak by the rock at the north end

bali-keramas.description: A powerful, short right over shallow volcanic reef in front of the Komune hotel — barrels from the very first stroke and one or two sections for turns. It works in the rainy season (November–March), when offshore westerlies blow on the east coast while the west of Bali suffers from onshore. Experienced surfers only — especially regular-footers.
bali-keramas.rating_basis: A fast, barrelling right-hand reef and a WSL event venue (Oakley Pro Bali, Corona Bali Protected); guides call it Bali's top wave in the rainy season. Surf-forecast reviews ~4/5; downsides — crowds and a tough queue
bali-keramas.hazards: Shallow, sharp volcanic reef (don't paddle out until at least an hour after low tide), heavy barrels and broken boards, current at the end of the wave, reef cuts, murky water after downpours
bali-keramas.crowd_note: In the rainy season, when the west coast is blown out, all the island's best surfers converge here. Quieter early in the morning and on weekdays; there are night sessions under the Komune hotel floodlights (booking required)
bali-keramas.region: Southeast coast of Bali (Gianyar), Badung Strait
bali-keramas.area_breaks: Nearby: Cucukan (smaller right-hand reef, takes some of the crowd), Lebih / Black Magic Point (shallow lava slab), Ketewel and Padang Galak (beach breaks), Sanur reef and Tanjung reef (40 min by boat, rainy season), Nusa Dua and Serangan
pros: Bali's best wave in the rainy season
Barrel and a canvas for turns on the same wave
Night sessions under floodlights
Closer to Ubud and Sanur than the Bukit
cons: Shallow, sharp reef, dangerous at low tide
Packed, competitive line-up
From May to September the trade wind blows onshore
Not for beginners or most goofy-footers

bali-uluwatu.description: A legendary left-hand reef beneath the cliff by Uluwatu temple: several sections (Temples, The Peak, Racetracks, Outside Corner, Bombie) work from 1 to 5+ m. In the dry season the trade wind blows offshore, and S swells from the Roaring Forties arrive almost daily. You paddle out through the famous cave. For confident intermediates and up — beginners have no business here.
bali-uluwatu.rating_basis: One of the world's best-known waves: a long left-hand reef with several sections and a WSL event (Uluwatu Pro); it makes every Indonesian top list. Downsides in reviews — constant crowds and cliquey locals
bali-uluwatu.hazards: Sharp reef and rocks (especially Racetracks at low tide and the end of the wave at The Peak), strong currents that sweep you past the cave on big days, a tricky exit at high tide, broken boards and big sets, coral cuts, sea urchins
bali-uluwatu.crowd_note: Crowded almost always, especially at The Peak and when the waves are small; Temples and Racetracks are usually quieter at high tide. Calmer early in the morning and in the shoulder seasons (April–May, September–October)
bali-uluwatu.region: Bukit Peninsula, southwest Bali, Indian Ocean
bali-uluwatu.area_breaks: Nearby on the Bukit: Padang Padang (left-hand barrel, experts; Padang Right for beginners), Impossibles, Bingin (short barrelling left), Dreamland and Balangan (softer, for intermediates), Nyang Nyang (exposed reef, picks up any swell)
pros: Very consistent swell in April–October
World-class long, powerful lefts
Dozens of other Bukit breaks 10–20 minutes away
Developed infrastructure: cafés above the line-up, rental, board repair
cons: Constant crowds and competition for waves
Sharp, shallow reef, especially at low tide (Racetracks)
From December to February the west monsoon blows onshore
Not for beginners

java-g-land.description: G-Land is a long left-hand reef on the jungle edge of Alas Purwo National Park in southeast Java. In the dry season the trade wind blows dead offshore, and S swells peel into walls and barrels hundreds of metres long. You can only stay in the surf camps on the shore (no village or roads), and people usually get there by boat or by transfer from Bali.
java-g-land.rating_basis: An Indonesian classic since the 1970s: a left-hand reef over a kilometre long, whose Money Trees and Speedies sections are among the best barrels in the world; guides (Wikipedia, The Surf Atlas, mondo.surf) call it a “must” for experienced surfers. Downside — it's remote and camp-only
java-g-land.hazards: Shallow, sharp reef (especially Speedies and Money Trees at low tide), sea urchins, strong currents along the reef, far from hospitals; in the national park jungle — monkeys, snakes, mosquitoes (dengue/malaria)
java-g-land.crowd_note: People spread out along the long reef, and the crowd depends on how full the camps are; Money Trees gets a bit packed at the peak of a swell, Kongs and Chickens are quieter
java-g-land.region: East Java, Alas Purwo National Park (Banyuwangi), Grajagan Bay
java-g-land.area_breaks: Reef sections: Kongs (walls, the easiest, works on small swell), Money Trees (long barrel, the main peak), Launching Pads, Speedies (the heaviest and shallowest barrel); softer — Chickens, 20/20s (left and right), Tiger Tracks. In the off-season (late November–April) — Reverse G, a right ~30 km to the east (by boat)
pros: Some of the longest and most perfect left-hand barrels in the world
Steady offshore in the dry season
No village — just jungle and ocean
Smaller crowds than Bali
cons: Confident intermediates and experienced surfers only
Camps close in the rainy season
Half a day's journey from Bali
Shallow reef and serious injuries at Speedies
java-g-land.airport: DPS — Denpasar (Bali): overland with a ferry across the strait — about half a day, or by boat from Bali; closer — BWX Banyuwangi

lombok-kuta-gerupuk.description: The village of Kuta in southern Lombok is a laid-back alternative to Bali, surrounded by a dozen reefs and beaches for every level. The main zone is Gerupuk bay, where boat taxis take you out to the breaks: the inner reefs are gentle and sheltered from the wind, the outer ones more powerful. The best season is the dry one (April–October), but there are waves year-round.
lombok-kuta-gerupuk.rating_basis: Guides (The Surf Atlas, Southeast Asia Backpacker, Wave Explorers) call it one of Indonesia's best zones for beginners and intermediates: a sheltered bay with several reefs for different levels, plus expert waves (Desert Point, Mawi) on the island. Downsides — crowds at Inside, a boat ride to the breaks
lombok-kuta-gerupuk.hazards: Shallow coral reef at low tide, sea urchins, flying boards in the Inside crowd, heavy sets at Outside, currents at exposed spots (Are Guling)
lombok-kuta-gerupuk.crowd_note: In season Inside Right is the island's most crowded line-up (50–100 people when it's small, and schools enjoy unspoken priority); Don Don, Outside Left, Ekas and Seger are noticeably quieter
lombok-kuta-gerupuk.region: South coast of Lombok (Central Lombok), Indian Ocean
lombok-kuta-gerupuk.area_breaks: In Gerupuk bay: Inside Right (beginners), Kiddies, Don Don (A-frame), Outside Right (intermediates), Outside Left (experienced). Nearby: Tanjung Aan and Batu Payung, Seger reef by Kuta, Mawi (barrels, intermediate+), Selong Belanak (sandy beach for learning), Ekas (Inside/Outside); far to the west — Desert Point (experts, dry season)
lombok-kuta-gerupuk.beginner_months: Best in May–September: lessons at Inside Right in Gerupuk bay, at Tanjung Aan and on Selong Belanak beach; in the rainy season the waves are less consistent, but schools run year-round
pros: Breaks for all levels in one bay
Calmer and cheaper than Bali
Sandy beaches for first lessons (Selong Belanak)
Waves year-round
cons: Gerupuk's breaks are reachable only by boat (~100,000 IDR for 2 hours)
Very crowded at Inside Right
Shallow reef at low tide
From midday the trade wind spoils the waves at exposed spots
lombok-kuta-gerupuk.best_wind_dir: N–NE (morning offshore; the bay is sheltered from the trade wind)

mentawai-macaronis.description: Macaronis is a left-hand reef on North Pagai island and one of Indonesia's best-known and most “user-friendly” waves: a long, even wall with a barrel at the start and an open shoulder. You get there either on a charter yacht (one to two weeks touring the archipelago's breaks) or by staying at the surf resort right in the bay. It suits strong intermediates on head-high days and experienced surfers on a big swell.
mentawai-macaronis.rating_basis: Surfertoday and surf guides call it one of the best waves in the world: a mechanically perfect left with a barrel and a long shoulder that works on any tide. The Mentawais as a whole are the benchmark boat surf trip
mentawai-macaronis.hazards: Sharp, shallow coral on the inside section (bring booties and a first-aid kit for cuts), a heavy take-off on double-overhead days, far from hospitals, malaria and dengue
mentawai-macaronis.crowd_note: Access is by booking: under Mentawai authority rules, 2 charter boats plus the resort guests are allowed at Macaronis at any one time, but the rule isn't always enforced. In April–October there are lots of boats; in December–February the line-ups are almost empty
mentawai-macaronis.region: Mentawai Islands (North Pagai, Pasongan bay), West Sumatra, Indian Ocean
mentawai-macaronis.area_breaks: In Pasongan bay: Mini Macas (left, intermediates), Macaronis Right (short barrelling right), Fish Fingers (beach for beginners). In the southern Mentawais: Greenbush, Rags Right/Left, Thunders, Roxys; in the north of the archipelago — Lance's Right (HT's), Lance's Left, Rifles, Telescopes, Bank Vaults
pros: One of the best lefts in the world
Works on any tide and in various winds
The boat limit keeps the crowd in check
Dozens of world-class breaks around
cons: Expensive: charter or resort, everything prepaid
Long journey via Padang and across the sea
Sharp, shallow reef on the inside section
Malaria area, medical care is far away
mentawai-macaronis.airport: PDG — Padang (Minangkabau); then ferry or speedboat to Sikakap / overnight crossing on a charter yacht

bundoran-the-peak.description: Bundoran is a small resort town in northwest Ireland and the heart of Irish surfing. The Peak is an A-frame over rock reef right by the town promenade: it works at low tide on a westerly swell, with a fast, barrelling left and a longer, softer right. The cold water and wind are made up for by powerful Atlantic swell and a friendly atmosphere.
bundoran-the-peak.rating_basis: Ireland's surf capital: The Peak is a quality A-frame reef (the left fast and steep, the right holding any size) and a venue for European and national championships. Thesurfatlas notes a friendly if busy line-up; downsides — cold water and windy weather
bundoran-the-peak.hazards: Shallow rock reef (especially at dead low tide), close-outs on the left on a big swell, strong winds and storms in winter, hypothermia
bundoran-the-peak.crowd_note: There are always people at The Peak when it's working, but the vibe is friendly; Tullan Strand, Rossnowlagh and the Sligo beaches are noticeably quieter
bundoran-the-peak.region: County Donegal, northwest Ireland (Atlantic, Donegal Bay)
bundoran-the-peak.area_breaks: Nearby: Tullan Strand (3 km beach, all levels, a longboard A-frame by the Rougey rocks), Bundoran main beach (shorebreak), Rossnowlagh (15 km, beginners), Mullaghmore Head (15 km, world-class tow-in big wave), Streedagh Strand (Sligo), Easkey (60 km, left and right reefs)
bundoran-the-peak.beginner_months: May–September: lessons on Tullan Strand north of town (sand, works on any tide) and at Rossnowlagh (15 km); schools are packed in summer — book ahead. The Peak reef itself is off-limits for beginners
pros: Quality reef within the town
Lots of spots within 20 km, including the Mullaghmore big wave
Friendly locals and Irish pubs
Consistent Atlantic swell in autumn and winter
cons: Very cold water (10–16 °C), in winter you need a 5/4 with booties, gloves and a hood
Frequent strong W–SW wind and rain
The Peak only works at low tide
Far from major airports
bundoran-the-peak.airport: NOC — Ireland West (Knock), ~1 h 30 min; BFS — Belfast, ~2 h 30 min; DUB — Dublin, ~3 h

tel-aviv-hilton.description: City surfing on the Tel Aviv waterfront: at Hilton Beach two jetties shape A-frames over a mix of reef and sand. The best time is November to March, when Mediterranean storms bring swell up to 1.5–2 m and there's sometimes an easterly offshore; in summer there's a small wind swell almost daily and pool-like water — easy for learning. The swells are short-lived: you have to catch them on day one according to the forecast.
tel-aviv-hilton.rating_basis: Israel's best-known surf spot (Surfertoday, Culture Trip, Time Out): A-frames between two jetties right in the city and a strong surf culture; but Mediterranean swell fades fast — Surf-forecast gives it 2/10 and “inconsistent”
tel-aviv-hilton.hazards: Rocks and concrete jetties, currents by the breakwaters, crowds; jellyfish swarms in summer (June–July); water pollution after downpours; check safety advisories before you travel
tel-aviv-hilton.crowd_note: When there are waves, Hilton is very crowded — it's the main city spot; quieter at Maaravi, in Jaffa and on the beaches to the north (Herzliya, Netanya)
tel-aviv-hilton.area_breaks: Gordon and Frishman (beach breaks, schools), Dolphinarium, Maaravi (exposed beach to the south, lefts and rights by stone pillars, big in winter), Jaffa; Herzliya and Netanya (Kontiki, Sironit) to the north; Bat Galim in Haifa (~95 km, several peaks for longboarding and intermediates, rocks)
tel-aviv-hilton.beginner_months: May–October: a small NW wind swell, knee- to waist-high, and warm water at 22–29 °C; lessons at Hilton Beach, Gordon Beach and Maaravi (Jaffa), and in winter in the mornings and on small days
pros: Surfing right in a big city, everything close by
Warm water most of the year
Plenty of schools and rentals
In summer there's almost always a small wave for learning
cons: Swell is inconsistent and fades quickly
Very crowded on the main peaks
Waves are small for experienced surfers
Unstable security situation in the region

kerala-varkala.description: The beaches below Varkala's red cliffs are a warm (28–30 °C), laid-back place for first lessons, with yoga and Ayurveda thrown in. The season runs from October to April: small, consistent SW swells, glassy or light offshore mornings, and a sea breeze picking up by midday. From June to September the monsoon brings storms and dangerous seas.
kerala-varkala.rating_basis: Lonely Planet and Kerala Tourism call Varkala and Kovalam the main surf spots of southern India; the waves are small and soft — good for learning (Surf-forecast: “crowds are never a problem”, but wave quality 1/10); for intermediates the Edava left-hand point and Kovalam by the lighthouse are more interesting
kerala-varkala.hazards: Strong rip currents and backwash (swimmers regularly drown on Varkala's beaches), shifting sandbars, dirty water after rain, heat and sun; stormy seas in the monsoon
kerala-varkala.crowd_note: Visiting surfers number in the hundreds along the whole coast, so the line-up is uncrowded; a bit busier on the left-hand point at Edava
kerala-varkala.area_breaks: North Cliff and Black Beach (Varkala), Odayam, Edava (fast, barrelling left-hand point by the mosque, intermediate+), Kappil, Paravur (A-frame at the river mouth); Kovalam (~50 km south: left-hand point by the lighthouse and Hawa Beach) and Poovar (powerful left, seasonal)
kerala-varkala.beginner_months: October–April on the beaches below Varkala's cliff, North Cliff and Black Beach, and at Kovalam (Hawa Beach); best to surf early in the morning before the sea breeze. In the monsoon (June–September) the sea is rough — off-season
pros: Very warm water, no wetsuit needed
Soft waves for beginners, hardly any crowds
Inexpensive, yoga and Ayurveda
Convenient Trivandrum airport nearby
cons: Small waves, quality days are infrequent
Onshore by midday
The June–September monsoon is off-season
Dirty water in places, conservative dress code away from the tourist beaches
kerala-varkala.airport: TRV — Thiruvananthapuram (Trivandrum), ~1 h to Varkala, ~30 min to Kovalam

chiba-ichinomiya-tsurigasaki.description: Ichinomiya is a surf town on the east coast of the Boso Peninsula, an hour to an hour and a half from Tokyo; Tsurigasaki beach hosted Olympic surfing in 2021. Sandbars between rock groynes produce peaks breaking left and right; the best waves come with typhoons in August–October, while winter brings consistent swell and an offshore NW wind, but cold water.
chiba-ichinomiya-tsurigasaki.rating_basis: Japan's best-known surf beach and the venue of the first Olympic surfing competition (Tokyo 2020, July 2021). Japanesetaste calls Tsurigasaki a “popular and reliable” spot for all levels; the waves break on sandbars by rock groynes, with the best days delivered by typhoon swells
chiba-ichinomiya-tsurigasaki.hazards: Rips by the rock groynes, powerful typhoon swells (August–October), cold water in winter; follow local beach rules and the queue
chiba-ichinomiya-tsurigasaki.crowd_note: Very crowded at weekends, especially in summer (Tokyo is 1–1.5 h away); noticeably quieter on weekdays and in winter
chiba-ichinomiya-tsurigasaki.region: Chiba Prefecture, Boso Peninsula (Kujukuri coast), Pacific Ocean
chiba-ichinomiya-tsurigasaki.area_breaks: Along Kujukuri beach: Shidashita and Taito (beach breaks by the groynes), Torami (next to Ichinomiya); further south — Onjuku (gentle waves, beginners, families) and Katsuura (fewer people)
chiba-ichinomiya-tsurigasaki.beginner_months: Learning is easiest from June to early September (warm water, small waves) on the beaches of Ichinomiya and Onjuku; in autumn, on typhoon swells, beginners should pick sheltered stretches by the breakwaters
pros: The closest serious surf area to Tokyo
Waves almost year-round
Olympic beach with surf shops, rentals and cafés
Suits all levels on different stretches
cons: Crowded at weekends
Cold water in winter (14–15 °C) — a 4/3–5/4 wetsuit needed
Waves depend heavily on typhoons
Little information and few schools in English, none in Russian
chiba-ichinomiya-tsurigasaki.airport: NRT — Tokyo Narita, ~1 h; HND — Haneda, ~1.5 h

sri-lanka-arugam-bay.description: Arugam Bay is the surf capital of eastern Sri Lanka: a right-hand point at the south end of the bay and a dozen or so rights along the coast. The season is April–September, when the SW monsoon blows offshore here while the south of the island is shut down. A relaxed village with hostels, cafés and schools; good for intermediates.
sri-lanka-arugam-bay.rating_basis: The main surf resort of eastern Sri Lanka and the country's best-known right: a long point with rides of 150–400 m. Guides (The Surf Atlas, yamu.lk) call it the best Sri Lankan destination in summer; downside — crowds in June–August
sri-lanka-arugam-bay.hazards: Rocks and reef on the point, crowds and flying boards; crocodiles in the lagoons near Peanut Farm and Elephant Rock; wild elephants on the roads in the evening; currents off the headlands (Okanda)
sri-lanka-arugam-bay.crowd_note: Main Point is very crowded in June–August; Peanut Farm is the schools' base; Okanda, Lighthouse and Pottuvil Point are quieter. Fewer people in April–May and September–October
sri-lanka-arugam-bay.region: East coast (Ampara, Pottuvil), Bay of Bengal / Indian Ocean
sri-lanka-arugam-bay.area_breaks: Nearby: Baby Point (soft inside section, beginners), Peanut Farm (right-hand points, beginner–intermediate, ~20 min south), Elephant Rock (soft longboard wave), Pottuvil Point (long sandy point), Lighthouse (two rights, ~45 min north), Whiskey Point (weakened by erosion), Okanda (three points, strong intermediate+, 23 km south)
sri-lanka-arugam-bay.beginner_months: May–September: lessons at Baby Point (the inside of Main Point), Peanut Farm on small days and Elephant Rock; beginners have an easier start in the south of the island in winter
pros: Long rights — heaven for regular-footers
In season when the south of Sri Lanka isn't working
Lots of breaks for different levels within 30 km
Inexpensive accommodation and a surf-village vibe
cons: Crowds at Main Point in summer
Barely works from December to March (NE monsoon)
Long drive from Colombo
Hardly any lefts
sri-lanka-arugam-bay.airport: CMB — Colombo (Bandaranaike), ~7–8 h by car; closer — domestic flights to Ampara / Batticaloa (BTC)

sri-lanka-weligama.description: Weligama is a long sandy bay in southern Sri Lanka and the island's main place to learn to surf. From November to April the NE monsoon blows offshore, and small SW swells produce soft, gentle waves where beginners get to their feet. All around there are dozens of schools and camps, many with Russian-speaking instructors, and 10–30 minutes away are the reefs of Midigama and Mirissa and Hiriketiya bay for intermediates.
sri-lanka-weligama.rating_basis: Sri Lanka's most popular place to learn and the island's “Russian surf capital”: dozens of schools and camps (including Russian-speaking ones). The wave itself is modest (Surf-forecast ~2/5), but there are reefs for intermediates nearby — Mirissa, Midigama, Rams
sri-lanka-weligama.hazards: Crowds of beginners and flying boards, polluted water in part of the bay, currents on big summer swells; on the neighbouring reefs (Midigama, Mirissa) — shallow reef, coral and sea urchins
sri-lanka-weligama.crowd_note: Dozens of students and schools in the bay at any one time, especially in December–March; the Midigama reefs and Hiriketiya are also busy at the height of the season, quieter early in the morning
sri-lanka-weligama.area_breaks: Nearby: Mirissa (left-hand reef and Mirissa Right, intermediates), Madiha and Rams (reefs for experienced surfers), Midigama (Lazy Left/Lazy Right, Coconut Point, Plantation), Ahangama and Kabalana (beach and reef); ~30 km east — Hiriketiya (horseshoe bay: left-hand reef and a soft beach break, all levels)
sri-lanka-weligama.beginner_months: November–April is the best season for learning: soft waves in the sandy bay almost every day, with the tide making little difference. Schools run in summer too, but the waves are bigger and the wind is onshore
pros: Ideal for first lessons: sand, soft waves
A great many Russian-speaking schools and camps
Reefs for intermediates 10–30 minutes away
Inexpensive accommodation and food, warm water year-round

The wave in the bay itself is weak for experienced surfers
June to September brings SW monsoon onshore and storms
The water in the bay is dirty in places (fishing harbour, run-off)
sri-lanka-weligama.airport: CMB — Colombo (Bandaranaike), ~2.5–3 h via the expressway; HRI — Mattala, ~1.5 h

imsouane-the-bay.description: Imsouane is a fishing village on a headland between Agadir and Essaouira. The Bay is a soft right that wraps around the point and runs across the entire bay: on a long-period swell rides reach 600–800 m, and you can walk back along the beach. The best conditions are from October to March, when NW swells arrive and the trade winds ease.
imsouane-the-bay.rating_basis: “One of the longest waves in Africa” (Surfertoday): rides of 600–800 m; Thesurfatlas — “probably the best longboard point in Africa”. Popular with beginners and longboarders; for shortboarding on a big swell it's sectiony
imsouane-the-bay.hazards: Rocks at the paddle-out to the line-up (especially at low tide), sea urchins, collisions with longboards in the crowd, currents at Cathedral
imsouane-the-bay.crowd_note: In season The Bay has lots of longboarders and camp groups, but it's still calmer than Taghazout; the line-up is smaller in summer
imsouane-the-bay.area_breaks: Nearby: Cathedral (right-hand point and a beach with peaks both ways on the north side of the headland, faster and more powerful — intermediate+), the reef between The Bay and Cathedral (hollow waves for advanced surfers); Tamri and the Taghazout points are 50–80 km to the south
imsouane-the-bay.beginner_months: Year-round: on small days the soft wave deep in The Bay and Cathedral beach (at high tide) are ideal for learning and longboarding; in summer the waves are smaller, but the bay is sheltered from the northerly wind
pros: One of the longest waves in Europe and Africa
Ideal for longboarding and progressing surfers
Easy paddle-out via the channel and from the beach
Quiet village, fresh fish; Russian-speaking camps in Taghazout run surf trips here

Far from the airport, hard to reach without a car

taghazout-anchor-point.description: Anchor Point is a long right peeling along a rocky headland a kilometre from Taghazout village, the signature wave of Moroccan surfing. From October to March winter NW swells deliver section after section, and the area has a dozen points and beaches for every level. A warm, dry winter climate, inexpensive camps and Moroccan cuisine make Taghazout one of Europeans' top winter surf destinations.
taghazout-anchor-point.rating_basis: Morocco's best-known wave: Thesurfatlas — “a world-class right-hand point”, long walls up to 500 m (mondo.surf), holds 2–3 m swell and more; Taghazout is North Africa's main surf hub, with dozens of camps. Downside — heavy crowds on the take-off
taghazout-anchor-point.hazards: Rocks when entering and exiting off the point (often sea urchins — bring reef booties), a steep, tight take-off, crowds, currents on a big swell
taghazout-anchor-point.crowd_note: Up to 30 people on the take-off on a good day; quieter at the neighbouring points (Hash Point, Mysteries, Boilers) and early in the morning
taghazout-anchor-point.area_breaks: Nearby: Killer Point (powerful right, experts), Boilers (right by a shipwreck), Mysteries, Hash Point (soft right, all levels), Panoramas (inside section of Anchor), La Source (reef), Banana Point and Devil's Rock (beginners, Tamraght/Aourir), Crocro; Imsouane is 80 km to the north
taghazout-anchor-point.beginner_months: Year-round, especially May–September (0.5–1.5 m waves): lessons in Tamraght and Aourir — Banana Point, Devil's Rock, Crocro; in winter on small days — Hash Point and the inside section at Panoramas. Anchor Point itself is for confident intermediates and up
pros: A long, world-class quality right
Warm, sunny winter (+21–24 °C)

taghazout-anchor-point.airport: AGA — Agadir, ~45 min (40 km); RAK — Marrakech, ~3 h

madagascar-anakao.description: A Vezo fishing village on Madagascar's dry southwest coast: just offshore, on the outer reefs and around Nosy Ve island, long lefts and the occasional right break. The season runs from April to October, when S swells roll in from the Southern Ocean and an easterly offshore blows in the mornings (the wind picks up during the day). You reach the peaks in fishermen's boats; there's nothing here for beginners, but the water is warm and there's almost nobody around.
madagascar-anakao.rating_basis: Surf Atlas and Détours Madagascar call the reefs off Anakao the island's main surf area: Flameballs is “a fast, long, international-class left” with hardly any crowd; Surf-forecast notes the “very consistent” Jelly Babies (up to 57% clean days in July). Downsides — remoteness, boat-only access, sharks
madagascar-anakao.hazards: Shallow, sharp coral and rocks, sharks (especially near river mouths), strong wind in the afternoon, far from medical help, cyclones from November to March; malaria
madagascar-anakao.crowd_note: The line-ups are almost always empty — only a handful of surf lodges and guides operate in the area
madagascar-anakao.region: Southwest Madagascar (Atsimo-Andrefana region, near Toliara), Mozambique Channel
madagascar-anakao.area_breaks: Flameballs (long left north of Nosy Ve island, experienced surfers, boat access only), Jelly Babies (reef with rights and lefts off the southern tip of Anakao), Puss Puss (outer reef, quickly blown out by the wind); further south — Lavanono (left over coral, ~250 km from Fort Dauphin)
pros: Quality reef lefts with no crowds
Warm water 23–27 °C
Consistent S swell in season
Wild nature and Vezo culture

Almost no infrastructure, rentals or schools
Boat-only access to the peaks
November–March is cyclone season
madagascar-anakao.airport: TLE — Toliara (Tuléar), then ~1 h by boat; international flights via TNR Antananarivo

mauritius-tamarin-bay.description: Tamarin is a classic left over reef at a river mouth on the dry west coast; it works best in the southern winter (May–September) on SW swells with the SE trade wind, which blows offshore here. The bay is sheltered and needs a big swell, so the wave is inconsistent. For experts the island's top prize is One Eye at the foot of Le Morne mountain.
mauritius-tamarin-bay.rating_basis: Mauritius's best-known wave (the film “Forgotten Island of Santosha”, 1974): Surf-forecast gives it the island's highest rating of 5/10, but “inconsistent”; Lonely Planet and Air Mauritius rank Tamarin and One Eye among the island's top spots; for experts — One Eye at Le Morne (4/10, “consistent”, up to 71% clean days in May)
mauritius-tamarin-bay.hazards: Shallow, sharp reef and coral, sea urchins, strong currents in the passes (especially at One Eye), localism; sharks are rare
mauritius-tamarin-bay.crowd_note: When the bay is working, locals gather on the single peak — space is tight; One Eye can get crowded too, while the other reefs are usually empty
mauritius-tamarin-bay.region: West coast (Black River district), Indian Ocean
mauritius-tamarin-bay.area_breaks: One Eye at Le Morne (~17 km, powerful left through a reef pass, experts only, blown out in strong wind), Le Morne lagoon (beginners), Rivière des Galets (lefts, pebbles), Manawa and Baie des Oursins in the south (reefs, experienced surfers)
mauritius-tamarin-bay.beginner_months: Small waves near shore in Tamarin bay itself and around Le Morne (fewer rocks) — local schools teach year-round, more comfortable in October–April when the swell is weaker
pros: Warm water 23–28 °C, boardshorts are fine
The trade wind blows offshore on the west coast
A resort with good hotels and a kite lagoon nearby
One Eye nearby — a world-class wave for experts

Shallow reef and few peaks — crowded with locals

maldives-north-male-sultans.description: North Malé Atoll is the most accessible surf area in the Maldives: a dozen reef waves 20–60 minutes by boat from the airport. Sultans is a long, fast right on the outer reef of uninhabited Thanburudhoo island; it works on any tide and holds a big swell. Access is by boat only: from resorts, from guesthouses on Thulusdhoo and Himmafushi, or on a surf charter.
maldives-north-male-sultans.rating_basis: Surfertoday and amaldives call Sultans one of the most consistent waves in the Maldives: a long right that “never closes out”; Malé Atoll is the country's most accessible surf area, with a dozen world-class reefs. Downsides — crowds in May–August and high prices
maldives-north-male-sultans.hazards: Shallow, sharp coral (reef booties needed), coral cuts that quickly get infected in warm water, currents on a big swell, far from hospitals, strong sun
maldives-north-male-sultans.crowd_note: At the height of the season (May–August) Sultans and Chickens get crowded: boats from resorts, charters and Thulusdhoo guesthouses; at weekends locals from Malé. Honky's and Lohis are usually quieter, and Pasta Point is for guests of the Dhonveli resort only
maldives-north-male-sultans.region: Kaafu Atoll (North Malé), Thanburudhoo island, Indian Ocean
maldives-north-male-sultans.area_breaks: Nearby: Honky's (long left on the other side of Thanburudhoo, works when Sultans is onshore), Jailbreaks (long right off Himmafushi), Cokes (powerful barrelling right off Thulusdhoo), Chickens (long left off Kuda Villingili), Lohis and Pasta Point (lefts, resort-exclusive); further south — South Malé Atoll (Kandooma and others)
pros: Perfect reef waves in warm, clear water
Just 20–60 minutes from the airport
Options from guesthouses to charters and resorts
Honky's and Sultans complement each other in different winds
cons: Expensive (boats, resorts, charters)

From December to February the waves are small and infrequent
maldives-north-male-sultans.airport: MLE — Malé (Velana), 20–60 min by boat to the breaks

puerto-escondido-zicatela.description: Puerto Escondido is Oaxaca's main surf town and the world capital of heavy beach breaks. Zicatela throws powerful, hollow barrels right by the shore on SW swells; in the S swell season (April–October) waves reach 4–8 m. Intermediates surf the left-hand point at La Punta, beginners the coves of Carrizalillo and Marinero.
puerto-escondido-zicatela.rating_basis: The “Mexican Pipeline” — one of the heaviest beach breaks in the world, with a WSL Big Wave event and the Puerto Escondido Challenge; it features in world top lists (Surfertoday, Surfline, The Surf Atlas). For intermediates the rating is backed up by La Punta, but the main peak is for experts only
puerto-escondido-zicatela.hazards: Heavy shorebreak and close-outs, strong rip currents, broken boards and injuries; rocks at La Punta; sharks at times; petty theft on the beach
puerto-escondido-zicatela.crowd_note: On big days Zicatela has few people out (too scary), while La Punta and Carrizalillo are very crowded: La Punta is tight with rocks nearby, and Carrizalillo has up to 30 people in a small cove
puerto-escondido-zicatela.area_breaks: Nearby: La Punta (long left by the rocks, intermediates), Carrizalillo (soft wave in a cove, beginners), Playa Marinero (beginners), Bacocho (beach break), Punta Colorada (point to the north, advanced); further south — Chacahua and Barra de Colotepec
puerto-escondido-zicatela.beginner_months: Zicatela itself is off-limits for beginners. Lessons run year-round in Carrizalillo cove and at Playa Marinero; the best months for learning are December–April, when the swell is smaller and cleaner. Intermediates surf the La Punta left-hand point at the south end of Zicatela
pros: Waves year-round, very consistent
Warm water 27–29 °C, no wetsuit needed
Options for all levels in one town
Inexpensive, social scene and beachside accommodation
cons: The main peak is deadly for the unprepared

puerto-escondido-zicatela.airport: PXM — Puerto Escondido, ~10 min; HUX — Huatulco, ~2 h

sayulita.description: Sayulita is a hippie town on the Riviera Nayarit and one of the main places in Mexico to learn to surf. In front of town there's a right-hand point by the river mouth and a soft left-hand beach break over sand; the wave is slow and forgiving. Winter (November–May) brings small clean waves and dry weather; in summer the S swells are bigger, but it's hot and rainy, and the water by the river is murky.
sayulita.rating_basis: One of the most popular places to learn in Mexico (Rapture Camps, Mexico Travel & Leisure, The Surf Atlas): a soft, slow wave, a right-hand point and a left-hand beach break, and a bohemian town. Advanced surfers find few waves and head to Punta Mita and La Lancha; downsides — crowds and murky water after rain
sayulita.hazards: Rocks and pebbles at the point (footwear needed), collisions in the crowd, currents on big summer swells, murky water and rubbish at the river mouth after downpours, jellyfish; hurricane season June–November
sayulita.crowd_note: From December to March the line-up is packed with schools and board renters; San Pancho (7 km north) has a fraction of the people
sayulita.region: Nayarit, Riviera Nayarit (north of Puerto Vallarta)
sayulita.area_breaks: Nearby: Punta Sayulita (reef to the south), La Lancha (faster, with barrels, intermediate/advanced, ~3 km), San Pancho (beach break, lefts, ~7 km), the Punta Mita points — El Faro, La Lancia, Stinky's, Burros (25 km, best on N swells in November–May)
sayulita.beginner_months: November–May is the best time to learn: 0.6–1.2 m waves, dry and sunny; lessons right on the main beach (the left over sand), with fewer people in April–May

Waves almost year-round
Lots of schools and rentals, a lively town

tofo-tofinho.description: A laid-back village on a headland near Inhambane: at the south end of the beach is the Tofinho right-hand point over reef, with powerful walls and short barrels, and on the beach itself a beach break for learning. The best time is April–August, when S swells arrive and a westerly offshore blows in the mornings. The water is warm year-round, and between sessions you can swim with whale sharks and manta rays.
tofo-tofinho.rating_basis: Tofinho is a quality right-hand reef point (Surf-forecast 4/10, “very rarely crowded”); Surfertoday and Surf Atlas call Tofo Mozambique's main surf spot; plus warm water and whale sharks, minus inconsistency and tricky logistics
tofo-tofinho.hazards: Reef and rocks at Tofinho, close-outs on the beach break, currents, sharks (rich marine life), seasonal jellyfish; malaria — prophylaxis needed
tofo-tofinho.crowd_note: Almost always uncrowded: Tofinho usually has a few locals and travellers, and only gets busy during South African holidays (December, Easter)
tofo-tofinho.area_breaks: Nearby: Tofo main beach (beach break, beginners), Barra (on the headland, works only on a big S swell); Guinjata Bay (right-hand walls for all levels, ~1 h 15 min drive)
tofo-tofinho.beginner_months: Year-round on Tofo's main beach (0.5–1.2 m beach break, with a peak by the jetty), best on a small swell in the morning; lessons are given by local dive centres and surf shops
pros: Warm water year-round
Hardly any crowds
Whale sharks, manta rays and humpback whales (June–October)
Backpacker-village vibe, inexpensive

Tricky logistics: flights via Johannesburg, bad roads

tofo-tofinho.airport: INH — Inhambane, ~30 min (flights from Johannesburg); MPM — Maputo, ~7–8 h by car

skeleton-bay-namibia.description: A fast, shallow and extremely long left-hand barrel along a sand spit northwest of Walvis Bay in the middle of the Namib Desert. It only works in the southern winter (May–September) on a big, long-period SW swell — usually for 1–3 days in a row, so people come here on purpose for a specific forecast. Experts only: the wave breaks on almost dry sand, and the current sweeps you down the point.
skeleton-bay-namibia.rating_basis: The longest sand-bottom left-hand barrel in the world (up to ~2 km, rides of up to 3 minutes): No. 1 on Surf Europe's list of the world's longest waves, a regular star of Stab and Surfertoday, and once discussed as a WSL venue; but it works only a few days a season and is for experts only
skeleton-bay-namibia.hazards: Very shallow (breaks on ankle-deep sand) — injuries and broken boards; strong current along the spit (~20 km/h), a long walk back up to the peak (driving back is banned by local rules); a seal colony at Pelican Point and murky water — shark risk; jellyfish; cold water at 14–17 °C, fog, wind and dust
skeleton-bay-namibia.crowd_note: When the swell arrives, “strike missions” fly in from around the world — dozens of the best surfers on the peak, and only a small fraction catch a wave of their own; empty the rest of the time
skeleton-bay-namibia.area_breaks: The wave itself runs along the Pelican Point sand spit; the Swakopmund beach breaks (~35 km north) are for mellower surfing

Sand bottom (not reef)
Desert scenery and seals
When it's on — several barrels in a single ride

skeleton-bay-namibia.airport: WVB — Walvis Bay, ~45 min by 4x4; WDH — Windhoek, ~5–6 h by car

popoyo-main-reef.description: Popoyo is a surf village on Nicaragua's Emerald Coast, known for a rare natural phenomenon: a warm wind off the huge Lake Nicaragua blows offshore most of the year. Main Reef is an A-frame peak over a rock slab with hollow lefts and rights that works on any tide; 150 m further out is Outer Reef for big-wave surfing. All around there are a dozen beaches and reefs for every level.
popoyo-main-reef.rating_basis: Nicaragua's best-known and most consistent spot: “over 300 days of offshore a year” thanks to the wind off Lake Nicaragua (Mondo Surf, Perfect Wave, The Surf Atlas — “a real gem for upper intermediates”). Outer Reef holds waves of 6–8 m. Downside — Popoyo hasn't been a secret for a long time, and crowds are growing
popoyo-main-reef.hazards: Rock reef (shallow at Outer Reef, lots of injuries), currents and backwash, strong offshore gusts in December–March, sun; the country's political situation — check entry rules
popoyo-main-reef.crowd_note: In season (May–September) Main Reef has lots of camps and boats from San Juan del Sur; Playa Santana, Guasacate and Beginner Bay are quieter
popoyo-main-reef.region: Rivas Department, Emerald Coast, Pacific Ocean
popoyo-main-reef.area_breaks: Nearby: Outer Reef (heavy left for experts, from 3–4 m), Playa Guasacate (beach break, sand), Beginner Bay (beginners), Stoneys (point), Playa Santana and Rancho Santana, Panga Drops, La Bocana (river mouth, sandy A-frames); further south, near San Juan del Sur — Playa Maderas, Remanso, Mayal, Colorados
popoyo-main-reef.beginner_months: December–March: smaller swell (northwesterly), lessons at Beginner Bay (sand) and on Playa Guasacate; in summer beginners are better off on inside waves and in coves

Very consistent waves, works on any tide
Lots of breaks of different levels nearby
Cheaper than Costa Rica

popoyo-main-reef.airport: MGA — Managua, ~2.5 h; LIR — Liberia (Costa Rica), ~3 h including the border crossing

raglan-manu-bay.description: Raglan is New Zealand's surf capital, with three left-hand points in a row. Manu Bay is the closest to town: a fast take-off, a barrel and then a long 300+ m wall over boulders, coming alive on SW swells that wrap around the headland. The best time is autumn and winter (March–August); the water is cool, so you need a 3/2–4/3 wetsuit.
raglan-manu-bay.rating_basis: New Zealand's most famous point: a long left featured in the film “The Endless Summer” (1966); together with Whale Bay and Indicators it's one of the best chains of left-hand points in the world (Surfertoday, The Surf Atlas). Downsides — crowds on the best swells and localism
raglan-manu-bay.hazards: Rocks and boulders on the bottom (booties essential), a heavy take-off and fast sections at Indicators, currents on a big swell, a hidden boulder at Whale Bay at high tide, cold water
raglan-manu-bay.crowd_note: Manu Bay is the most crowded of the three points, especially at weekends and during the summer holidays; Whale Bay is quieter, and Indicators is for strong surfers
raglan-manu-bay.region: North Island, Waikato region, west coast (Tasman Sea)
raglan-manu-bay.area_breaks: Nearby: Whale Bay (the softest of the lefts, intermediates), Indicators (the longest and fastest left, strong intermediates and experts), Boneyards, Ngarunui Beach (sand, beginners), Wainui and Ruapuke (beaches), Te Akau and the Raglan Bar (north shore), Albatross Point (left, access needed, heavy localism)
raglan-manu-bay.beginner_months: Lessons run year-round on the sandy beaches of Ngarunui (5 min from Manu Bay) and Wainui; in summer (December–March) the water is warmer and the waves softer — the best time for first lessons

Three points for every level from intermediate up
Consistent swell from the Tasman Sea
Atmospheric surf town, beaches for learning nearby

raglan-manu-bay.airport: AKL — Auckland, ~2–2.5 h; HLZ — Hamilton, ~45 min

santa-catalina-la-punta.description: Santa Catalina is a quiet fishing village on Panama's Pacific coast and the gateway to Coiba marine park. The main wave is La Punta: a powerful right (with a short left) over uneven reef that holds up to 4 m and works on almost any S swell. The season is April–October; in the dry season the waves are smaller but cleaner. There's excellent diving here too.
santa-catalina-la-punta.rating_basis: Many guides rate it Panama's best wave (The Surf Atlas — “the money wave”, Mondo Surf, Visit Panama): a powerful right over reef that works on any S swell. Downsides — a crowded line-up in season, a tough journey and shallow reef at low tide
santa-catalina-la-punta.hazards: Uneven, shallow reef and rocks (a repair kit and reef booties are a must), sea urchins, tricky entry and exit at low tide, strong sun
santa-catalina-la-punta.crowd_note: La Punta gets crowded in season (one peak, lots of camps and longboarders); Playa Estero, Punta Brava and Punta Roca are almost empty
santa-catalina-la-punta.region: Veraguas province, Pacific coast (near Coiba National Park)
santa-catalina-la-punta.area_breaks: Nearby: Playa Estero (beach break, beginner–intermediate), Punta Roca (reef, left, upper intermediate), Punta Brava (short lefts, at low tide), Catalina island, and across the bay — Morrillo (hollow rights, by boat)
santa-catalina-la-punta.beginner_months: Year-round on the sandy beach break at Playa Estero (10 min from the village), best in December–March when the swell is smaller. La Punta is off-limits for beginners — shallow reef

Warm water, no wetsuit

chicama-puerto-malabrigo.description: Chicama is a legendary left-hand point by the village of Puerto Malabrigo in the Peruvian desert, the longest surfable wave on the planet. On a good SW swell the wave runs along the headland through several sections; you get back by walking along the shore or on a tow boat. The season is April–October, and the water is cold because of the Humboldt Current.
chicama-puerto-malabrigo.rating_basis: The longest left in the world — up to 2–4 km when the sections link up (Surfertoday, NASA Earth Observatory, Wavetribe); a cult spot for intermediates, where you can do dozens of turns on a single wave. Downsides — inconsistency (it needs a good S swell), cold water and desert remoteness
chicama-puerto-malabrigo.hazards: Rocks and reefs at low tide (especially at Keys), sea urchins, a strong current along the point (paddling back is pointless), close-outs on the sandbars at El Point, cold fog; don't drink tap water
chicama-puerto-malabrigo.crowd_note: Usually uncrowded — the line-up stretches over kilometres; it gets busy when only El Point or Malpaso is working
chicama-puerto-malabrigo.region: La Libertad region, northern Peru (≈70 km from Trujillo)
chicama-puerto-malabrigo.area_breaks: Sections of the same wave: Malpaso (outer, the most powerful), La Isla/El Cape, Keys (by the rock, experienced surfers), El Point (the main one, intermediates), El Hombre, El Pueblo (by the pier). Nearby: Pacasmayo (long left, ~40 km north), Huanchaco (left over sand, a World Surfing Reserve, ~70 km south)
chicama-puerto-malabrigo.beginner_months: On small days (more often from November to March) beginners and confident novices learn on the El Point section with an instructor; schools and rentals are in the village. The nearest town for learning is Huanchaco (beach break over sand)

Almost constant offshore

mancora-point.description: Máncora is a party beach town in sunny northern Peru that people visit for warm water and consistent small waves. The main point is a soft left over cobblestones, good for learning and progressing; in summer (December–March) NW swells work, in winter S swells. It's a convenient base for trips to the world-class lefts of Lobitos and the Cabo Blanco barrel.
mancora-point.rating_basis: Peru's most popular beach and surf resort: a soft left-hand point for beginners and intermediates, warm water and sun year-round (The Surf Atlas, Surf-forecast, Culture Trip). In quality it's “a baby compared to Chicama”, but the world-class lefts of Lobitos and Cabo Blanco are nearby
mancora-point.hazards: Cobblestones on the bottom at the point, currents on big swells, crowds on the peak; shallow reef at Cabo Blanco
mancora-point.crowd_note: When it's working the point is crowded (schools, tourists), especially from December to March and on holidays; Vichayito and Los Organitos are quieter
mancora-point.region: Piura region, far north of Peru
mancora-point.area_breaks: Nearby: Punta Ballenas (slab, advanced), Pocitas and Vichayito (soft peaks, beginners), Los Organitos/Punta Veleros (left), Los Órganos; ~30–60 km away — Cabo Blanco (heavy barrel, experts, winter to summer on NW swells) and Lobitos (several left-hand points, intermediate+)
mancora-point.beginner_months: Year-round; most comfortable in December–March (warm water, sun). Lessons on the shoulder of the point, on Pocitas beach and the Vichayito beach breaks

siargao-cloud-9.description: Cloud 9 is a fast, hollow right over shallow reef by the famous wooden pier on Siargao's east coast. The best time is August–November, when the SW monsoon blows offshore and Pacific and typhoon swells produce waves up to double overhead. The island itself centres on the laid-back surf village of General Luna, with schools and soft spots for beginners.
siargao-cloud-9.rating_basis: The Philippines' best-known wave: a fast, barrelling right by the wooden pier and the annual international Siargao Cloud 9 Cup (late October–November). Surf-forecast reviews ~4/5; guides call it an “expert wave”, and among the downsides is “Crowd 9” at the height of the season
siargao-cloud-9.hazards: Very shallow, sharp reef (dangerous at low tide, reef booties needed), strong currents in the line-up, crowds; at neighbouring spots — sea urchins, rocks in the channel (Stimpy's), currents at Rock Island; typhoons (September–December)
siargao-cloud-9.crowd_note: Cloud 9 is crowded in September–November and during the contest; quieter before dawn. There are reefs with smaller crowds (Stimpy's, Tuason), and boats run out to Daku and Rock Island
siargao-cloud-9.region: Siargao Island (General Luna), Surigao del Norte, Philippine Sea / Pacific Ocean
siargao-cloud-9.area_breaks: Nearby: Jacking Horse (soft right, schools), Quiksilver (the island's toughest wave, barrels), Stimpy's (quality left), Tuason (steep wall), Rock Island and Daku (by boat; Daku is a soft right for intermediates), Cemetery (peaky reef), Pacifico (north of the island)
siargao-cloud-9.beginner_months: You can learn year-round at Jacking Horse near General Luna (soft right on mid and high tide); in summer (April–July) the waves are small and glassy — the best time for beginners, while in autumn beginners should stick to the school spots
