rincon-puerto-rico-domes.description: Rincón is a town on Puerto Rico's northwest tip, where NW Atlantic swells arrive in winter. Domes is a reef peak by the dome of the former BONUS nuclear plant, with rights and lefts; nearby are the Maria's right and the Tres Palmas big wave. The season is October–March, the water is warm year-round; entry requires a US visa.
rincon-puerto-rico-domes.rating_basis: The Caribbean's main surf capital: the 1968 world championship and dozens of reefs and points within 10 minutes of each other (The Surf Atlas, Lonely Planet, 57hours). Tres Palmas is the Caribbean's big wave. Downsides — inconsistency outside winter and shallow reefs
rincon-puerto-rico-domes.hazards: Shallow reefs and rocks, sea urchins, rip currents (especially at Antonio's), powerful waves on big swells; hurricanes in summer
rincon-puerto-rico-domes.crowd_note: Domes and Maria's are crowded on good days; October and March are quieter than the peak of winter. Sandy Beach is busy with schools
rincon-puerto-rico-domes.region: Northwest coast of Puerto Rico, Caribbean
rincon-puerto-rico-domes.area_breaks: Nearby: Maria's (right over reef, all levels on small days), Indicators, Point Higuero (big waves), Tres Palmas (big wave, experts), Dogman's (right, advanced), Steps, Pools and Sandy Beach (beginners), Antonio's; to the north — Arecibo, Aguadilla (Crash Boat, Wilderness, Surfer's Beach)
rincon-puerto-rico-domes.beginner_months: October–April at Sandy Beach (sand, long lefts) and on the inside waves at Maria's on small days; there are almost no waves in summer
pros: Lots of reefs and points in a small area
Warm water year-round
Relaxed atmosphere, developed infrastructure
Offshore trade wind at Maria's and Domes
cons: Inconsistent: depends on North Atlantic swells
Almost flat from May to August
Shallow, sharp reefs, urchins
You need a US visa and a car
rincon-puerto-rico-domes.airport: BQN — Aguadilla, ~30–40 min; SJU — San Juan, ~2 h

ericeira-ribeira-d-ilhas.description: A long right peeling along a rocky bay 3 km north of Ericeira — the signature wave of Portugal's surf capital. Ribeira d'Ilhas holds swell from 0.5 to 3+ m, works on any tide and is more forgiving than the neighbouring reefs. All around there's a whole collection of waves for every level, plus schools, camps and hostels, and Lisbon is 50 km away.
ericeira-ribeira-d-ilhas.rating_basis: One of Europe's best right-hand point breaks (Surfertoday) and a former WSL venue; Ericeira was Europe's first World Surfing Reserve (2011), with a dozen great reefs within a 10 km radius
ericeira-ribeira-d-ilhas.hazards: Rocks and reef in the line-up (especially at very low tide), rip currents on a big swell, sea urchins
ericeira-ribeira-d-ilhas.crowd_note: On good days and at weekends the line-up is packed and competitive, with lots of schools; quieter on weekday mornings and at the neighbouring reefs
ericeira-ribeira-d-ilhas.region: Lisbon coast, Atlantic (Ericeira World Surfing Reserve)
ericeira-ribeira-d-ilhas.area_breaks: Nearby: Coxos (powerful right-hand reef, advanced), Crazy Left and Pedra Branca (left-hand reefs), Reef and Cave (heavy barrels, pros), São Lourenço (right-hand reef for big swell), Foz do Lizandro and São Julião (beach breaks for beginners), Praia do Sul and Praia dos Pescadores (in town)
ericeira-ribeira-d-ilhas.beginner_months: May–September: smaller waves; beginners learn on the beaches of Foz do Lizandro, São Julião and Praia do Sul in Ericeira itself; the Ribeira point is only for those already confident on green waves
pros: A long, quality right
Lots of breaks for every level within 10 km
Developed infrastructure: schools, camps, rentals, shapers
Close to Lisbon, year-round surf
cons: Crowded and competitive on good days
Cold water (15–19 °C), a 3/2–4/3 wetsuit needed year-round
Waves are often weak in summer
Storms and SW onshore in winter

nazare-praia-do-norte.description: The Nazaré submarine canyon, up to 5 km deep, focuses winter storms, and waves 20–30 m high rise off the lighthouse headland. From October to March people come to watch the tow-in surfers from the Forte de São Miguel Arcanjo. Surfing Praia do Norte is for professionals with jet-ski support only; on small days it's a heavy beach break with close-outs.
nazare-praia-do-norte.rating_basis: The biggest waves ever surfed: Guinness records by Garrett McNamara (2011) and Sebastian Steudtner (26.2 m, 2020), and an annual WSL tow-in event. For the ordinary surf traveller it's above all a spectacle, not a place to surf
nazare-praia-do-norte.hazards: Deadly waves and currents, powerful shorebreak, close-outs; tourists have drowned on the beach — keep well away from the water and the cliff edge
nazare-praia-do-norte.crowd_note: Only pros on jet skis in the water; but on big days there are thousands of spectators on the headland by the lighthouse, and no parking
nazare-praia-do-norte.area_breaks: Nearby: Nazaré town beach (sheltered bay, punchy waves on a S swell), Praia do Sul (barrels on a big swell, pros), São Martinho do Porto (enclosed bay, beginners), Salgado and Vale Furado (beach breaks to the north)
nazare-praia-do-norte.beginner_months: Praia do Norte is off-limits for beginners and intermediates in any season. In summer people learn in the calm bay of São Martinho do Porto (13 km) or go to Peniche (40 km)
pros: The planet's greatest big-wave spectacle
A convenient viewing point by the lighthouse, a big-wave surfing museum in the fort
Peniche and calm bays nearby for regular surfing
cons: Only suitable for experts to surf
Giant days aren't guaranteed — you have to catch the forecast
Crowds of spectators and no parking on big days
Cold water
nazare-praia-do-norte.airport: LIS — Lisbon, ~1 h 15 min (120 km); OPO — Porto, ~2 h

peniche-supertubos.description: Peniche is a peninsula — almost an island — with beaches facing north, south and west, so there's nearly always somewhere to surf. Supertubos is a fast, barrelling wave over sand (the lefts are better) and a world championship venue; next door in Baleal is one of Europe's main “school” bays. A good choice both for a first trip and for progressing surfers.
peniche-supertubos.rating_basis: Supertubos is the “European Pipeline”, hosting a WSL Championship Tour event (MEO Rip Curl Pro Portugal) every October; Surfertoday calls it Europe's best barrel. With coastlines facing different directions, the peninsula offers a working spot in almost any wind
peniche-supertubos.hazards: Powerful barrels and close-outs over a shallow sandbar at Supertubos, rip currents, rocks at Consolação and Gigi, crowds in the line-up
peniche-supertubos.crowd_note: Supertubos is always busy when it's working; in summer Baleal has queues for lessons and crowds of schools. Areia Branca and Pico da Mota are noticeably quieter
peniche-supertubos.area_breaks: Nearby: Baleal (Cantinho da Baía and Baleal Sul — beach breaks for beginners; Baleal Norte), Lagide (left-hand reef), Molhe Leste (right by the harbour jetty, powerful barrels in winter), Consolação (rocky right-hand point, advanced), Papoa (big-wave reef), Prainha, Gigi, Pico da Mota, Areia Branca
peniche-supertubos.beginner_months: May–October: beginners learn in Baleal bay (Cantinho da Baía, Baleal Sul), at Prainha and at Areia Branca — sheltered from big swell and wind; Supertubos itself is for beginners only on the very smallest days
pros: Almost always a working spot thanks to coastlines facing different ways
World-class barrel at Supertubos
Baleal is ideal for learning
A huge choice of schools, camps and rentals
cons: Crowded at Supertubos and Baleal in summer
Cold water, a 3/2–4/3 wetsuit needed
Strong nortada (northerly wind) by midday in summer
Supertubos often closes out and slams onto the sand

sagres-tonel.description: Sagres is a surf village on the southwestern corner of Europe. Tonel is a beach below the cliffs by the fortress, open to westerly swell: on small days it suits progressing surfers, while winter swells bring powerful barrels and close-outs. The area's big advantage is that the west and south coasts are side by side: in storms and wind you can always move to the sheltered side.
sagres-tonel.rating_basis: Thesurfatlas and Rapture Camps: “at the edge of Europe” two coasts — west and south — give you a working spot in almost any wind and swell; over 20 spots within 10–20 km. Tonel itself is a reliable but not legendary beach break (rated 4/5 on Surf-forecast)
sagres-tonel.hazards: Strong rip currents (especially by the rock in the bay at low tide), hidden rocks at high tide, heavy close-outs on a big swell, sheer cliffs
sagres-tonel.crowd_note: Tonel and Mareta have lots of schools in season; the wild beaches of the west coast (Cordoama, Castelejo) are usually uncrowded
sagres-tonel.area_breaks: Nearby: Mareta (south-facing bay in town, beginners, works on a big NW swell), Beliche (reef/beach below cliffs, advanced, some localism), Martinhal, Zavial (10 km, quality wave, localism), Cordoama and Castelejo (wild west coast, swell magnets), Amado (25 km, surf-camp beach), Arrifana (40 km, beginner beach and a right-hand point under the cliff)
sagres-tonel.beginner_months: May–October: lessons on the west-coast beaches (Amado, Arrifana, Cordoama) and at Tonel on small days; in winter, when the swell is big, in the sheltered south-facing bay of Mareta right in Sagres
pros: Two coasts — almost always a working spot
The warmest, sunniest winter in Portugal
Lots of schools and camps, relaxed atmosphere
Wild, uncrowded beaches on the west coast
cons: Strong rip currents at Tonel
In summer the south coast is often flat, and the nortada blows out the west
Localism at Beliche and Zavial
Far from the airport, you need a car
sagres-tonel.airport: FAO — Faro, ~1 h 15 min (115 km); LIS — Lisbon, ~3 h

kaliningrad-zelenogradsk.description: A resort town at the start of the Curonian Spit and the surf capital of the Baltic: several schools and a year-round base with hot showers and rentals. The waves are wind swell driven by storms, so people surf strictly by the forecast; the strongest and most frequent storms come from September to January, while summer is more often flat, but the water is warm and good for learning. In winter the water is 2–5 °C, so you need a 5–6 mm wetsuit with booties and gloves.
kaliningrad-zelenogradsk.rating_basis: The most popular place to surf in European Russia (T—Zh, Vokrug Sveta, Aviasales, Tonkosti): well-developed schools and bases, but it's a sea wave — short, choppy and only in a storm; best in September–November
kaliningrad-zelenogradsk.hazards: Cold water and hypothermia in autumn–winter, strong storms and currents by the breakwaters, rocks at Donskoye; accidents on the Baltic more often involve drunk holidaymakers who don't know the sea
kaliningrad-zelenogradsk.crowd_note: On a stormy day the town peaks in Zelenogradsk get crowded (surfers come from all over the region); Donskoye, Yantarny and the Curonian Spit are quieter
kaliningrad-zelenogradsk.region: Kaliningrad Oblast, Baltic Sea (by the Curonian Spit)
kaliningrad-zelenogradsk.area_breaks: The Zelenogradsk town peaks and the Curonian Spit (beginners), Malinovka; on the west coast of the Sambia Peninsula — Svetlogorsk, Pionersky, Yantarny and Donskoye (rocky bottom, experienced surfers, almost deserted); the jetty in Baltiysk. Locals call the region's spots “Jack Spot”, “Ambar” (“Barn”) and “Koleso” (“Wheel”)
kaliningrad-zelenogradsk.beginner_months: June–September: water 15–19 °C, small waves, a gently sloping sandy entry — Zelenogradsk schools teach on days with a wind swell (there can also be weeks of flat calm)
pros: In Russia, with no visa or flights halfway around the world; sandy bottom
Well-developed Russian-speaking schools and rentals
Gently sloping entry — good for first lessons in summer
Lots of spots along the region's coast
cons: Short, choppy waves, only in storms
Often flat for weeks in summer
Cold water from November to May
Strong wind, often onshore

kamchatka-khalaktyrsky.description: A long beach of black volcanic sand at the foot of the Avachinsky and Koryaksky volcanoes, 30 minutes from Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky. Locals surf year-round, but the real season for travellers is July to October: the water is 10–13 °C, summer surf camps are open, and autumn Pacific storms bring the most consistent waves (the best month is September). In winter the water is around 0 °C, the air down to −15 °C, and sometimes you can only reach the ocean by snowmobile.
kamchatka-khalaktyrsky.rating_basis: Russia's main cold-water surf destination (T—Zh, Vokrug Sveta, Moscow Times, Swellnet): a real ocean wave, black volcanic sand and volcano views; Surf-forecast — 3/10, “not crowded even when it's working”, best month September (~54% clean days). Downsides — cold, changeable weather and expensive tickets
kamchatka-khalaktyrsky.hazards: Cold water and hypothermia, strong currents and rips, storms with sudden big sets, rapidly changing weather; bears and fur seals on the shore; far from settlements, tsunami risk; in autumn 2020 there was an environmental incident on the beach (mass die-off of marine life caused by a harmful algal bloom)
kamchatka-khalaktyrsky.crowd_note: The beach stretches for ~30 km and is almost always uncrowded; in summer it only gets busy by the camps on the central peaks (Halo Spot, “Tom Curren”, Central), where beginners learn
kamchatka-khalaktyrsky.area_breaks: Along Khalaktyrsky beach — the Halo Spot, “Tom Curren” and Central peaks; in the bays south of the entrance to Avacha Bay there are reef and point spots (rocks, experienced surfers, often need a boat or a 4x4)
kamchatka-khalaktyrsky.beginner_months: July–September with an instructor at a summer camp on Khalaktyrsky beach (5–6 mm wetsuit, booties, gloves); water 10–13 °C
pros: A real ocean wave in Russia, no international passport needed
An empty 30 km beach
Volcanoes, bears, orcas — unique nature
Russian-speaking schools and camps with rentals
cons: Cold water even in summer (10–13 °C), a thick wetsuit needed
Expensive flights and tours
Abruptly changing weather, fog
Short comfortable season
kamchatka-khalaktyrsky.airport: PKC — Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky (Yelizovo), ~1 h to the beach

sochi-khosta.description: The Khosta river mouth is Sochi's best-known surf spot: after autumn and winter storms, short peaks break here over pebbles and rocks. It's a Black Sea wind swell that only appears for 1–2 days after a storm, once the wind drops, so people surf strictly by the forecast; the best time is December to February. In summer the sea is usually calm — time for SUP and the artificial wave.
sochi-khosta.rating_basis: Sochi's main spot (Aviasales calls Khosta the city's “best place” to surf), but it's a Black Sea wave — wind-driven, short and only after a storm; T—Zh and Tonkosti note pebble beaches and strong currents, and the spots are small and crowded
sochi-khosta.hazards: Pebbles and rocks, concrete breakwaters and groynes, strong current in a storm (hard to paddle out to the line-up), rubbish and murky river water after downpours
sochi-khosta.crowd_note: The peaks are small, and on storm days every surfer in Sochi heads to Khosta — the line-up is crowded; Morvokzal, Mys Vidny, Adler and Imeretinka have local crews
sochi-khosta.area_breaks: Khosta Rica, Mandarin, Morvokzal and Riviera (central Sochi), Mys Vidny, Shirokaya Balka, Adler and Imeretinskaya Bay (~15 km south); the Wake People artificial wave by the Imeretinsky resort
sochi-khosta.beginner_months: September–October on small days after storms, with an instructor at the gentler spots (Imeretinskaya Bay); in summer there are few waves — beginners learn on the artificial wave or on a SUP
pros: Surfing next to the Krasnaya Polyana ski resort — waves in the morning, snow in the afternoon
Russian-speaking schools and rentals
Mild climate, water around 9–12 °C in winter
Easy to get to, direct flights
cons: Inconsistent waves, only after storms
Pebble and rocky bottom, not for complete beginners
Small, crowded spots
Strong currents on storm days

teriberka-barents-sea.description: Surfing on the edge of the Arctic: thanks to the warm North Cape (Murmansk) Current the Barents Sea doesn't freeze here, and autumn and winter storms bring N swells. Realistic times to go are September–November and March–May: December–January is polar night and the road can get snowed over, and summer has few waves. It's an expedition for experienced surfers with thick wetsuits — there are no schools or lifeguards, and conditions change every 10 minutes.
teriberka-barents-sea.rating_basis: An exotic trip for experienced surfers: Arctic surfing at Teriberka has featured in the Surf Siberia films and in Vokrug Sveta, T—Zh and OneTwoTrip; in May 2024 it hosted the first Murmansk Oblast surfing championship. The waves are inconsistent (storms change conditions within minutes), there are no schools, and the water is 2–10 °C
teriberka-barents-sea.hazards: Hypothermia and frostbite, strong current, rocks and submerged ledges, sudden storms, no rescue service; polar night in December–January; the only road closes in bad weather
teriberka-barents-sea.crowd_note: Just a handful of local surfers from Murmansk and the occasional expedition in the water; it never gets crowded
teriberka-barents-sea.region: Murmansk Oblast, Kola Peninsula, Barents Sea
teriberka-barents-sea.area_breaks: Sandy bays around Teriberka Bay and rocky spots along the coast (many reachable only on foot or by snowmobile); new spots are being found on the Rybachy Peninsula (~150 km to the west)
pros: Unique Arctic surfing and an empty line-up
Northern lights, whales, tundra
You can drive there from Murmansk
Polar day in spring — you can surf at night
cons: Water 2–10 °C, you need a 6–7 mm wetsuit, booties, gloves and a hood
No schools, rentals or lifeguards
Inconsistent waves and rapidly changing conditions
The road from Murmansk may close in a blizzard
teriberka-barents-sea.airport: MMK — Murmansk, ~120 km, 2–3 h by car

dakar-ngor-right.description: Dakar sits on the westernmost point of Africa and catches swell from two sides: in winter (November–March) NW swells light up the reefs of Ngor and Almadies, and in summer S swells work on the peninsula's south shore. The main wave is the right-hand reef off Ngor island, a 5-minute pirogue ride away. The water ranges from 19 °C in winter to 28 °C in summer, and the setting is a lively West African capital.
dakar-ngor-right.rating_basis: Ngor Right was made famous by the film “The Endless Summer” (1966); the peninsula catches swell from both north and south, so Dakar has waves almost year-round — Perfect Wave, Surf Simply and Surf Europe include it among the best winter surf trips; Surf-forecast — a “consistent” spot, 4/10
dakar-ngor-right.hazards: Sea urchins and rocks (especially at Vivier and Ngor Right), sharp reefs, currents on big swells, water pollution near city outfalls; a life jacket is a must on the pirogue to the island
dakar-ngor-right.crowd_note: Ngor Right can get crowded in winter (locals + guests from the surf camps on the island), while the dozens of reefs at Almadies and the coves at Les Virages are usually uncrowded
dakar-ngor-right.area_breaks: Ngor Left (softer, intermediates), Pointe des Almadies (a series of reefs), Ouakam (powerful barrelling wave by the mosque, experienced surfers, best on a S swell), Secret Spot, Les Virages (coves, beginners), Vivier (peaks, lots of urchins), Club Med, Yoff (beach break)
dakar-ngor-right.beginner_months: Year-round on the beach breaks at Yoff and Les Virages (small coves), best on a small swell; in summer (May–October) the waves are softer and the water warm
pros: Waves almost year-round
Lots of reefs and beaches on a small peninsula
Warm water in summer, a 2–3 mm is enough in winter
Short flight from Europe, vibrant culture
cons: Sea urchins and shallow reefs
City water is polluted in places
Summer (July–September) is the rainy season, hot and with fewer waves
A wetsuit is needed in winter — water 19–20 °C
dakar-ngor-right.airport: DSS — Dakar (Blaise Diagne), ~50 km, ~45–60 min to Ngor

el-salvador-punta-roca.description: The La Libertad coast, branded as Surf City, is a chain of right-hand points and reefs 40 minutes from the capital. Punta Roca is a fast, long right over boulders, one of the best rights in Central America and a WSL venue; 10 minutes away is party-town El Tunco with the La Bocana left and the mellow El Sunzal. Warm water, morning offshore, and big swells from March to October.
el-salvador-punta-roca.rating_basis: Punta Roca is “El Salvador's jewel”, a long right of up to 200–300 m and a WSL Championship Tour venue, Surf City El Salvador Pro (Surfertoday, Perfect Wave, The Surf Atlas). Nearby are long right-hand points for every level. Downsides — crowds, localism on the main peak and murky water near town
el-salvador-punta-roca.hazards: Boulders and rocks (including “Mama Roca” by the take-off at low tide), sea urchins, sharp barnacles, polluted water after rain, strong currents on big swells, petty theft
el-salvador-punta-roca.crowd_note: Punta Roca and La Bocana are usually crowded, with locals taking the best waves; El Sunzal and El Zonte are calmer, and Mizata is almost empty
el-salvador-punta-roca.region: La Libertad Department, Surf City, Pacific Ocean
el-salvador-punta-roca.area_breaks: Nearby: La Paz (inside section of Punta Roca, beginners), La Bocana (left-hand A-frame at the river mouth by El Tunco, advanced), El Sunzal (long, soft right, longboarding and intermediates), El Zonte (right-hand point, all levels), La Paz Beach, Mizata (reefs and points, empty, ~45 min)
el-salvador-punta-roca.beginner_months: November–February (dry season): waist-high waves, offshore — lessons on the La Paz inside section by Punta Roca, on the shoulders of El Sunzal and at El Zonte
pros: World-class long right-hand points
Warm water 27–30 °C
Lots of spots within 20 km, close to the airport
Inexpensive
cons: Crowds and localism at Punta Roca
Tricky entry and exit over boulders
Polluted water near La Libertad
Quickly onshore during the day

istanbul-kilyos.description: The sandy beaches of Kilyos, an hour from central Istanbul, are open to northerly Black Sea storms: from November to February waves from knee-high to 1.5 m and bigger arrive, often with offshore wind in the morning. The swell is short-period and lasts 1–2 days after a storm, so people surf by the forecast. In summer the NE wind turns the beach into a kite spot, and on small days schools teach beginners.
istanbul-kilyos.rating_basis: The closest surf to Istanbul: Chasing the Donkey and Oggusto call Kilyos and Şile the main spots on Turkey's Black Sea coast — waves from knee-high to 1.5 m+ in autumn and winter, offshore in the morning and onshore during the day; but the swell is short-period and storm-dependent
istanbul-kilyos.hazards: Strong rip currents and shorebreak — Istanbul's Black Sea beaches are known for swimmer drownings, and swimming bans apply in storms; cold water in winter
istanbul-kilyos.crowd_note: Few surfers — a local community from Istanbul; in summer the beach is packed with swimmers and kiters, in winter there's just a handful in the water
istanbul-kilyos.area_breaks: The neighbouring Kilyos beaches (Kumköy), Riva on the Asian shore (~30 km), Şile and Ağva (~70 km east, sandy beach breaks, several schools); Sinop — far to the east, for experienced surfers
istanbul-kilyos.beginner_months: Mid-May to October: warm water, and the summer NE wind (poyraz) produces a small wind swell — schools in Kilyos and Şile teach complete beginners on suitable days, best in the morning
pros: Surfing an hour from Istanbul and IST airport
Sandy bottom, schools and rentals available
Warm water in summer
Easy to combine with a city break
cons: Inconsistent, short-lived waves, only after storms
Cold in winter — water 8–12 °C
Often onshore during the day
Crowded beach in summer
istanbul-kilyos.airport: IST — Istanbul, ~35–45 min; SAW — Sabiha Gökçen, ~1.5 h

taiwan-jinzun.description: Jinzun is a scenic bay below cliffs on Taiwan's east coast that hosts a WSL event every November. A peaky right-hand point over pebbles and boulders works on winter NE swells and typhoon waves; nearby are the Donghe river mouth and several points for experienced surfers. Uncrowded, with warm water almost year-round.
taiwan-jinzun.rating_basis: An annual WSL event (Taiwan Open of Surfing, November; QS and longboard tours): the WSL calls the peaky boulder point one of the most consistent and “high-performance” waves in the region; Taiwan Outdoors — “one of Taiwan's best surf destinations”. There is little data on seasonality
taiwan-jinzun.hazards: Rocks and boulders on the bottom, currents at the points and river mouths (Baxiandong, Chenggong), typhoons (July–September, when surfing is banned)
taiwan-jinzun.crowd_note: Taiwan is one of Asia's least crowded surf destinations; Jinzun gets busy mainly during the November contest and at weekends
taiwan-jinzun.region: Taitung County, Donghe Township, east coast, Pacific Ocean
taiwan-jinzun.area_breaks: Nearby: the Donghe river mouth (left and right, consistent winter waves), Dulan (10 min south), Baxiandong (left-hand point by a river mouth, boulders, experienced surfers only), Chenggong (left-hand point over coral, strong current, experienced surfers)
taiwan-jinzun.beginner_months: Beginners are best off in March–April and September–October, when the waves are moderate and the water warm; in summer, during typhoons, surfing in Taiwan is banned by law
pros: Few people in the water
Warm water (over 20 °C in winter)
Beautiful wild coastline and surf hostels
A world-class contest wave
cons: Little information and few schools in English
Often small in spring and early summer
Surfing is banned during typhoons
Far from Taipei (train/flight to Taitung)
taiwan-jinzun.airport: TTT — Taitung, ~40–50 min; TPE — Taipei (Taoyuan), then train/flight
taiwan-jinzun.best_wind_dir: W (offshore); the bay is partly sheltered in the NE monsoon

malibu-first-point.description: Surfrider Beach in Malibu is the classic Californian right-hand point over cobbles and sand, where long, even waves run for up to 300 m. First Point is a soft longboard wave, while Second and Third Point are faster and suit shortboards. It works on summer and autumn S swells; in winter N swells barely get in.
malibu-first-point.rating_basis: One of the world's most famous longboard waves and the first World Surfing Reserve (2010); it features in US top lists (Lonely Planet, Surfertoday, The Surf Atlas). The downsides every review mentions are crowds, poor water quality after rain and inconsistency outside summer
malibu-first-point.hazards: Crowds and collisions, rocks at the point, sea urchins, polluted water after rain (run-off from Malibu Lagoon), cold currents in autumn
malibu-first-point.crowd_note: 40–100 people in the water in summer; lots of drop-ins and priority disputes. Quieter in autumn and at Zuma/County Line
malibu-first-point.area_breaks: Nearby: Second and Third Point (faster and hollow, shortboards), Topanga (right-hand point, crowded), Latigo, Point Dume, Zuma Beach (powerful beach break, winter–spring), Zero/Nicholas Canyon (left-hand point), Leo Carrillo (right-hand point on the tide), Staircase, County Line
malibu-first-point.beginner_months: First Point is too crowded and unsafe for beginners; in summer people learn on the soft inside waves by Malibu Pier and on the beaches at Zuma and Santa Monica (there are schools by the pier)
pros: A legendary long right for longboarding
The best months are warm summer and autumn
Los Angeles next door: accommodation, rentals, schools
Lots of other breaks within 20 km
cons: Extremely crowded
Poor water quality after rain and in the lagoon
Cold water — a 3/2–4/3 wetsuit needed
Hardly works in winter
malibu-first-point.best_wind_dir: N–NE (offshore); a light westerly breeze is OK

oahu-north-shore-pipeline.description: Oahu's North Shore is the world capital of winter surfing: from October to March powerful NW swells arrive from the North Pacific. Pipeline is a heavy, barrelling left (with the Backdoor right) over shallow, sharp reef with caves; it's a wave for experts and pros. For intermediates the coast has softer reefs — Chun's, Laniakea, Haleiwa — but even those can get serious in winter.
oahu-north-shore-pipeline.rating_basis: Pipeline is the world's most famous wave and the venue of a WSL Championship Tour event (Pipe Pro) and the Billabong Pipe Masters; the North Shore (the “seven-mile miracle”) features in every world top list (Surfertoday, Lonely Planet, Perfect Wave). For intermediates it's more a place to watch surfing than to surf the main peaks
oahu-north-shore-pipeline.hazards: Shallow, sharp reef with caves and ledges (fractures, lacerations), powerful heavy waves, strong rip currents, coral; on big swells it's extremely dangerous even for experienced surfers
oahu-north-shore-pipeline.crowd_note: In winter the Pipe line-up has dozens of pros, photographers and bodyboarders, with waves “allocated” by pecking order. Sunset Beach, Chun's Reef and Laniakea are slightly quieter, but still crowded
oahu-north-shore-pipeline.area_breaks: Nearby: Backdoor (right on the same reef), Off-the-Wall, Rockpiles, Sunset Beach (big right, experts), Waimea Bay (big wave, experts), Laniakea (right, intermediates), Chun's Reef (right, intermediates), Haleiwa (reefs, beginners on small days), Puaena Point (beginners)
oahu-north-shore-pipeline.beginner_months: Pipeline is not for beginners. In winter on small days lessons are held in Haleiwa bay (Ali'i Beach) and at Puaena Point; from May to September the North Shore is almost flat — beginners are better off in Waikiki on the south shore
pros: Legendary world-class waves and WSL contests
Consistent winter swells and an offshore trade wind
Warm water year-round — boardshorts are fine
Lots of breaks along 11 km of coast
cons: The main peaks are for experts only, with a strict pecking order and localism
Very expensive accommodation and car rental
Almost flat in summer
Dangerous: many injuries every year

waikiki-queens-canoes.description: Waikiki beach in Honolulu is the classic place to learn to surf: long, gentle waves break on the outer reef, and the offshore trade wind almost always keeps them clean. Queens is a soft right (with a short left) for longboarding, and Canoes is the friendliest wave for beginners. The season is the summer S swells from May to September.
waikiki-queens-canoes.rating_basis: The birthplace of modern surfing (Duke Kahanamoku) and one of the best places in the world to stand up on a board: long, soft waves over reef, warm water and dozens of schools (Surfertoday, Hawaii Guide, Hawaii Magazine). For experienced surfers it's more a longboard paradise than a place for serious waves; the main downside is the crowds
waikiki-queens-canoes.hazards: Shallow reef and coral at low tide, collisions with boards and canoes in the crowd; tiger sharks reported at Populars; sun
waikiki-queens-canoes.crowd_note: One of the most crowded places in the world: in the mornings hundreds of school students, longboarders, canoes and SUPs. Queens has a competitive line-up with local longboarders; Populars and Public Baths are quieter, but it's a long paddle out
waikiki-queens-canoes.area_breaks: Nearby: Queens (soft right, longboarding), Canoes (beginners), Populars and Public Baths (intermediates, long paddle), Walls (by the Kapahulu groin), Ala Moana Bowls (fast left, advanced), Diamond Head (intermediate/advanced), Sandy Beach (shorebreak, experts only)
waikiki-queens-canoes.beginner_months: Year-round at Canoes and on the inside waves by Kuhio Beach — even in winter there's usually a small wave to learn on; best from April to October, when the S swells arrive
pros: Ideal for learning and longboarding
Warm water year-round
Dozens of schools and rentals right on the beach
City, hotels and airport close by
cons: Very crowded in the water
Shallow reef at low tide
Usually small waves in winter
Expensive

da-nang-my-khe.description: My Khe is Da Nang's long sandy city beach and the most consistent surf spot in central Vietnam. From September to March the NE monsoon and typhoons bring a 0.5–1.5 m wind swell that's easy to learn on; in summer the sea is almost always calm. Easy to combine with a city break, Hoi An and the Ba Na Hills.
da-nang-my-khe.rating_basis: A simple sandy beach break with wind swell from the NE monsoon and occasional typhoon swells. The Surf Atlas gives the season as September–March (peak September–November) and praises the uncrowded line-up; the waves are inconsistent and short-period — a destination for beginners and surf holidays rather than a surf trip
da-nang-my-khe.hazards: Rip currents when the waves are big, shorebreak, typhoons (September–November), jellyfish, water pollution after downpours
da-nang-my-khe.crowd_note: The line-up is uncrowded and friendly even in season; on a typhoon swell Nam O can have a few dozen locals
da-nang-my-khe.region: Central Vietnam, Da Nang, South China Sea
da-nang-my-khe.area_breaks: Nearby: Nam O (left-hand point by the breakwater, intermediates, needs a big swell), Man Thai (sheltered beach, barrels at low tide on a big swell), Non Nuoc (sandy peaks, more powerful and windier), Hoi An — An Bang (small, soft waves, 30 km south)
da-nang-my-khe.beginner_months: September–March: the soft sandy beach break along the whole of My Khe beach is suitable for first lessons; in April–August it's almost always flat
pros: Soft sandy beach break for beginners
Uncrowded line-up
Airport, city and all the infrastructure close by
There's a Russian-speaking school
cons: Inconsistent, short-period, often windy waves
Almost flat from April to August
September–December is the rainy and typhoon season
Of little interest to experienced surfers
da-nang-my-khe.best_wind_dir: W–NW (offshore, rare); usually light wind in the morning

cape-town-muizenberg.description: Cape Town's top place to learn: a gently sloping sandy beach, long whitewater and soft waves in False Bay, with dozens of schools and rentals at Surfer's Corner. In winter (April–September) a NW offshore blows and consistent swell arrives; in summer mornings are calm and the wind picks up in the afternoon. More experienced surfers head to the Atlantic side of the peninsula — Long Beach in Kommetjie and dozens of other spots.
cape-town-muizenberg.rating_basis: Muizenberg itself offers soft, long whitewater and small waves (Surf-forecast rates its wave quality low, 2/10), but it's one of the best places in the world for first lessons; Cape Town as a whole ranks among the world's top surf cities (dozens of breaks, from Long Beach to the Dungeons big wave)
cape-town-muizenberg.hazards: Great white sharks in False Bay (spotters operate with flags and a siren), cold water, rip currents, powerful swell in winter; on the Atlantic side — kelp, rocks and water at 11–13 °C; petty theft
cape-town-muizenberg.crowd_note: Surfer's Corner gets busy in summer and at weekends (schools, rentals), but the long beach with several peaks spreads people out; quieter in winter. Long Beach in Kommetjie is crowded on a good day
cape-town-muizenberg.area_breaks: In False Bay: St James, Kalk Bay reef (powerful left over rocks, experienced surfers), Glen Corner. On the Atlantic side (20–35 km): Long Beach in Kommetjie (the best for intermediates, works in the SE wind in summer), Noordhoek, Scarborough, Llandudno, Glen Beach, Big Bay; Dungeons by Hout Bay — a big wave for pros
cape-town-muizenberg.beginner_months: Year-round at Surfer's Corner in Muizenberg; best in April–September (NW offshore, clean waves, fewer people). In summer (October–March) lessons are in the morning — in the afternoon the SE “Cape Doctor” blows
pros: Perfect beginner beach, lots of schools and rentals
A shark-watch service (Shark Spotters)
Cape Town: dozens of breaks for any wind and level within an hour's drive
A city with developed infrastructure and an exchange rate that favours tourists
cons: Cool water in winter (14–16 °C), 11–13 °C on the Atlantic side
Strong SE wind on summer afternoons
Muizenberg itself is a weak wave for advanced surfers
Security issues: theft, don't leave belongings on the beach

durban-new-pier.description: City surfing in the warm (21–26 °C) Indian Ocean: the piers along the beachfront shape sandbars with fast, barrelling peaks breaking both ways. The best season is the southern autumn and winter (March–September), when SSW swells arrive and a W–NW offshore blows; in summer the wind is more often NE, but there are waves almost all the time.
durban-new-pier.rating_basis: Durban is South Africa's “Surf City”: warm water year-round, dozens of peaks along the Golden Mile, and home to many champions (Jordy Smith); Surf-forecast — a “consistent” spot rated 4/10; downsides — city water and crowds
durban-new-pier.hazards: Sharks (the Golden Mile beaches are protected by KZN Sharks Board nets and drumlines), currents by the piers, jellyfish, water pollution after rain, theft on the beach
durban-new-pier.crowd_note: New Pier, Dairy Beach (Wedge) and North Beach get crowded on good days, especially at dawn and at weekends; Ansteys and the southern beaches are quieter
durban-new-pier.area_breaks: Along the Golden Mile: North Beach (intermediates), Bay of Plenty (consistent, contest venue), Dairy Beach / Wedge (holds big swell), Snake Park, Addington (beginners, longboarding), uShaka (complete beginners); further south — Ansteys and Cave Rock (powerful barrel over reef, experts only); further north — Umhlanga and Ballito
durban-new-pier.beginner_months: Year-round at Addington Beach and the most sheltered uShaka Beach (behind the breakwater), best on gentle days in the morning before the NE wind
pros: Warm water year-round, no wetsuit needed
Lots of peaks for every level right in the city
Waves almost every day
Inexpensive accommodation and an international airport nearby
cons: City water: pollution after downpours, beaches sometimes close
Localism and crowds at the best piers
High crime rate — don't leave belongings unattended
Frequent NE onshore in summer

jeffreys-bay-supertubes.description: A legendary right-hand point wave: on a S swell the Boneyards, Supertubes and Impossibles sections link up into a ride hundreds of metres long, with barrels. The best time is the southern winter (May–September), when Southern Ocean storms bring a consistent 1.5–3 m swell and a westerly offshore. In summer the waves are smaller and the wind is more often easterly, but you can surf and learn at The Point and Main Beach almost year-round.
jeffreys-bay-supertubes.rating_basis: One of the best right-hand point waves in the world: a WSL Championship Tour event (J-Bay Open) and a fixture of every top list (Surfline, Stab, Surf-forecast — a “very consistent” spot); downsides — crowds and sharks
jeffreys-bay-supertubes.hazards: Great white sharks (the famous attack on Mick Fanning during the 2015 WSL event), sharp rocks and mussels on the point, a strong current along the point, cold upwelling in summer; theft from cars
jeffreys-bay-supertubes.crowd_note: On a good swell Supertubes “rarely has fewer than 10 people on the peak”, and it's very crowded in winter and during the WSL event; The Point, Albatross and Main Beach are quieter
jeffreys-bay-supertubes.area_breaks: Along the point: Magna Tubes, Boneyards (top section, localism), Impossibles (pros only), Tubes, The Point (longboarding, intermediates), Albatross (the softest wave), Kitchen Windows (A-frame for intermediates), Main Beach (beginners); 20 km away — St Francis Bay (Bruce's Beauties, Gunnels)
jeffreys-bay-supertubes.beginner_months: Year-round on the sandy Main Beach / Dolphin Beach in the town centre, best in summer (November–March) when the waves are smaller; Supertubes is off-limits for beginners
pros: A world-class wave with very long rides
Almost never completely flat
Several sections for different levels in one place
Developed surf infrastructure and shapers, inexpensive accommodation
cons: Very crowded on the main peak
Sharks (great white)
Cool water — a 3/2–4/3 wetsuit needed
Far from an international airport
jeffreys-bay-supertubes.airport: PLZ — Gqeberha (Port Elizabeth), ~1 h (domestic flights via Johannesburg/Cape Town); from Cape Town (CPT) ~8 h by car
